videos.title: AI log analysis in EZ PM2 GUI
videos.description: An English walkthrough of connecting a remote server, reviewing a redacted log snapshot, choosing a provider, investigating cited evidence, and continuing a saved conversation. Sample logs and simulated analysis are clearly labeled.
videos.narration: A wall of logs can hide useful clues. E Z P M two G U I turns a snapshot into a focused conversation. This walkthrough uses sample logs and simulated analysis. Connect from the process sidebar. The list updates when the connection is ready. Open the service logs, then select Analyze logs to reveal the persistent right sidebar. Expand AI Settings and choose an available provider: Ollama local or cloud models, or an installed cloud-connected command-line provider. For cloud analysis, review the sharing notice and explicitly allow the snapshot and conversation to be sent. Inspect the redacted snapshot before sending it. The preview shows captured lines and limits. Ask a concrete question: why is this service restarting? Then start the analysis. The Markdown response appears separately from your question. Follow cited lines, distinguish observations from hypotheses, and review suggested checks. Verify the evidence before changing the application. Choose a suggested follow-up to fill the composer, then send it when ready. Requests and responses are saved in SQLite. Reopen your conversation from history and continue with the same context.

videos.title: Why EZ PM2 GUI uses TSLN
videos.description: An English explanation of the local TSLN log profile: adjacent repeated values, evidence preservation, redaction and round-trip verification, conditional JSON fallback, measured fixture bytes, and unchanged capture limits.
videos.narration: Logs can repeat timestamps, messages, and JSON field names hundreds of times. E Z P M two G U I uses a local T S L N based profile to reduce that repetition in AI prompts. T S L N means Time Series Lean Notation. Our profile declares the columns once, then writes one row per evidence line. An equals sign repeats the previous value in the same column. Every row, stream, and line number remains. Timestamps stay exact text, and the empty symbol marks an unparsed timestamp. Nothing is sorted, grouped, or dropped by compression, so repeated events remain countable. The backend redacts first. It encodes and decodes the candidate, verifies an exact match, then compares complete prompt representations. Compression is selected only for fewer UTF eight bytes; otherwise, JSON stays. Savings depend on the logs. Fewer bytes do not guarantee equivalent token savings. The captured tail stays bounded. Saved snapshots and the preview keep their original redacted rows. Open Help and demos for the implementation guide and the T S L N paper, published on engrXiv by Chandan Bhagat and Manas Mudbari.
